name: Uncooked to cooked rice
seoTitle: Uncooked to cooked rice Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Uncooked to cooked rice: work out cooked rice from the uncooked rice. A free food calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Uncooked to cooked rice calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports cooked rice immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. That makes it useful for portioning, timing or nutrition. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator work?
sections.html:
The Uncooked to cooked rice calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports cooked rice in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the uncooked rice.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in grams. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Cooked rice=3 × uncooked rice

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Uncooked rice = 10 g. Working through the relationship above gives Cooked rice = 30 g.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Cooked rice = 30 g should be roughly the size you expected from Uncooked rice = 10 g.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in grams, and convertible to any of the 3 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Rice measures, opening in grams
  • Rice measures, opening in grams

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Uncooked to cooked rice calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Scaling a recipe up or down
  • Working out timing so everything finishes together
  • Checking portions before you shop
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the uncooked rice — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — uncooked rice for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Switch the units to the ones you normally use and confirm the numbers are unchanged apart from their label; if they are not, a chip was on the wrong setting.

faq.q: What does the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns cooked rice, derived from the uncooked rice. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the uncooked rice, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter uncooked rice in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Uncooked rice opens in grams and the chip beside it offers 3 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Cooked rice = 30 g. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Uncooked to cooked rice calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
